description.en-US:
Your alarm always sounds the same, so you sleep right through it. And "just ten more minutes" on the sofa turns into midnight again. chaos-alert nags you to bed when it's time, gives you one word to remember, and wakes you with a sound you never hear coming. To turn the alarm off, you recall last night's word. A wrong pick only drops out, and the app keeps count of how well you remembered. What it does
  • Bedtime nag — at bedtime a quiet full-screen popup asks: Are you in bed? Bedtime follows from tomorrow's first alarm and how much sleep you want. Not yet? Snooze 10 minutes, or 30 min, 1 h, 2 h when you're out. Fell asleep without answering? The popup's time counts as your bedtime and nothing wakes you. Each popup also makes its case first, with one of 300 lines about sleep, dreams, puffy eyes, the Matrix and fairy tales.
  • In bed early — the main screen offers "I'm in bed" in the six hours before bedtime. Lying awake for a while? The nag asks "Want the word now?", or tap "Show the word" when you're ready to sleep.
  • A word for the night — one English word, shown once: a less common one, or a simple one if you choose.
  • The chaos alarm — every ring picks something random: an alarm sound, a notification sound, a song from your music, a sound from a folder you picked, or a mix of instruments the app makes itself. Each source has its own switch. Quiet at first, louder after 10 seconds, a new surprise after every snooze.
  • The quiz — four kinds to choose from. First letters, the default: three rounds of big tiles, each one letter more of the word's beginning, a tap answers. Whole word: last night's word among four. Broken teeth: four words of the same length with the same letters missing. Type it, the hardest: type the word in; up to two typos pass, with no second try. A wrong pick drops out while the alarm keeps ringing; after a night with wrong picks you see how many tries it took, your streak and your last 30 nights. Five failures in a row bring a gentle hint.
  • I'm awake — awake before the alarm? In the six hours before it, a button takes you to the quiz, and in the last hour a silent notification too. The alarm still rings with a plain turn-off that marks when you got up, or tap "I'm up" to end the night. Snoozed by mistake? "I'm awake" stays, and the right word ends the alarm there and then.
  • Alarms — repeating on weekdays or once on a date; reminder alarms that shouldn't move your bedtime simply get their wake-up switch turned off.
  • Vacations — enter the dates once; repeating alarms and the nag stay quiet, one-time alarms still ring.
  • Time in bed — a week or a month of bars, coloured by how the quiz went and dimmed where you lay awake, with your average time in bed, time asleep and bedtime.
Everything stays on your phone: no account, no internet permission, no tracking. Free and open source.

Old Brain Fix is a note and reminder app for Android. A desktop app for Linux, Windows and macOS uses the same data. There is no account and no server; all data is stored on the user's own devices. Capture • Text, photo and voice Notes, opened from the + button, home-screen widgets, Quick Settings tiles, app shortcuts, or a hardware button where the phone allows assigning one. • Content shared from other apps is saved as a Note. • Each Note records the time of capture. Optional: the location (shown as a Named Place such as "Home" when one matches), the current calendar event and the connected Bluetooth device. • Voice Notes are transcribed on the device with Whisper (English and German). The speech model (148 MB) is downloaded once, on request. • Text in photos and screenshots is recognised on the device with RustO, German letters and the euro sign included. • Transcripts and recognised text are included in search. Organising • New Notes are kept in Unsorted. A notification (Nudge) reports Unsorted Notes at a set interval; Quiet Hours suppress it at night. • Notes are filed into Areas and Topics (two levels), each with a colour and an icon. A starter set of Areas is offered at first start. • Notes can be edited, amended and merged. Deleted items stay in the trash for 30 days. • A Note can become a Checklist, a Shopping List whose items come back after a set number of days, weeks, months or years, a Tally with entries and charts, or a Session that picks Tallies. Its text can be formatted with headings, lists, tables, code blocks, boxes to tick and links that open other Notes and places in the app. Routines and Reminders • Any Note can have Reminders (one time) and Routines (repeating by a recurrence rule, several times a day if needed). • Alarms ring at the exact minute, also on the lock screen, and are restored after a restart. This requires the "Alarms & reminders" permission. • An alarm that is neither marked Done nor snoozed rings again at a set interval (Re-nag, default 10 minutes). Optionally, after a set number of repeats it is shown as a full-screen alarm with sound. • The Agenda lists today's Routines and Reminders, missed ones and the number of Unsorted Notes. It is also available as a home-screen widget. • Each Routine has a history with streak and adherence. • Routines and Reminders can be written to a device calendar or exported as an ICS file. Sync and sharing • Phone and desktop sync directly over the local network (TLS, paired by QR code or typed code), through a shared folder such as Syncthing or Nextcloud (end-to-end encrypted), or through an encrypted file sent with any app. • A single Area can be shared with another person. Other Areas are not shared. • Your Profile unites all of your Devices. Your name, a unique code and an optional picture show on the Notes you share with others. • A Note can be sent to another person as a file, together with its Routines and Reminders. The receiver can accept or decline it. • Notes, Topics or whole Areas can be handed to others as a Pack of copies, which they keep as their own. Privacy and security • No account, no server, no analytics, no advertising. • The app uses the network only for sync and for the speech model download. • Optional App Lock (PIN, fingerprint) and Area Locks. Capture and alarms keep working while locked. • Encrypted Backups (Argon2id, XChaCha20-Poly1305) into a chosen folder, optionally weekly, with a printable Recovery Sheet. Optionally, Android's backup to Google stores the encrypted Backup file and nothing else. Other • English and German. Light and dark theme. • Free and open source, licensed under Apache-2.0 or MIT.
